title: Quasi-excellence on affine charts of formal completions
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], meaning one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and assume that every affine open of $X$ has quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Form $\mathfrak X=\widehat X_{\mathcal I}$ by gluing $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I$ on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, where $I=\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ and $\widehat A_I=\varprojlim_n A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For a complete Noetherian ring $R$ with ideal of definition $K$, $\operatorname{Spf}R$ is the ringed space of primes containing $K$, with structure sheaf the inverse limit of the structure sheaves of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K^n)$. A formal affine open means an open ringed subspace isomorphic to such a $\operatorname{Spf}R$. Then $\mathfrak X$ is a Noetherian adic formal scheme, and for every formal affine open $\operatorname{Spf}R\subseteq\mathfrak X$ the ring $R$ is Noetherian and quasi-excellent. In particular, if $A$ is Noetherian and quasi-excellent and $I\subseteq A$ is any ideal, then $\widehat A_I$ and the rings on all formal affine opens of $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I$ are quasi-excellent. No regular morphism is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ from the Noetherian hypothesis. Each $A_i$ is Noetherian and each $I_i=\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)$ is finitely generated. Put $C_i=\widehat{A_i}_{I_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $C_i$ is Noetherian, complete for $I_iC_i$, and $C_i/I_iC_i\cong A_i/I_i$. Apply [lem-per-formal-completion-reduction-dictionary] to glue these charts and obtain the coherent ideal of definition $\mathfrak J$ and scheme quotient $Z=X_1$. The charts cover $|Z|=|\mathfrak X|$ and there are finitely many of them, so $\mathfrak X$ is Noetherian adic (a finite cover by complete Noetherian formal spectra).

For every $i$, $A_i$ is quasi-excellent by hypothesis. Set $B_i=A_i/I_i$, the coordinate ring of the corresponding affine open of $Z$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. The quotient map is of finite type, generated by the empty list; since $A_i$ is a G-ring, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] makes $B_i$ a G-ring. To check J-2, let $D$ be any finite type $B_i$-algebra. Its finite list of algebra generators also generates it over $A_i$, because $A_i\to B_i$ is surjective. Hence the J-2 property of $A_i$ says that the regular locus of $D$ is open. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] this proves J-2 and quasi-excellence for $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, quotient case; Tag 07PV; algebra.tex Tag 00FN

proof.text: The spectra of the $B_i$ cover $Z$ by Step 1. Their rings are Noetherian, so $Z$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] to this cover to see that the ring of every affine open of $Z$ is a G-ring. Apply [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] to the same cover and the established local Noetherianity to get J-2 for every such ring. By [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] a G-ring is already Noetherian, and [def-exc-excellent-ring] says these conditions give quasi-excellence of the ring on every affine open of $Z$. No intersections of affine opens were assumed affine.

proof.text: Let $U=\operatorname{Spf}R$ be any formal affine open of $\mathfrak X$. In the statement this means that $R$ is a complete Noetherian adic ring. The quotient dictionary [lem-per-formal-completion-reduction-dictionary] supplies an ideal $J\subseteq R$ such that $R$ is $J$-adically complete and $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ is the open subscheme of $Z$ on $|U|$. In particular this open subscheme is affine, even when $U$ is contained in none of the originally chosen charts. Step 3 therefore gives quasi-excellence of $R/J$. The hypotheses of [lem-per-gabber-adic-quasi-excellence] now hold for $(R,J)$, so $R$ is quasi-excellent. This checks arbitrary formal affine opens, rather than only completed principal opens.

source.place: Exposé I Théorème 9.2, printed p.17; Temkin §2.4.3 for the formal-geometric application

proof.text: For the last assertion let $A$ be Noetherian and quasi-excellent, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathcal I=\widetilde I$. The single chart shows that $X$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The sheaf $\widetilde I$ is quasi-coherent, and finitely many generators of $I$ give a surjection $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\widetilde I$, so it is of finite type. Hence it is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and $\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}A)=I$. The hypothesis on all affine opens holds: $A$ is a G-ring, hence Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], so the cover $\{\operatorname{Spec}A\}$ with [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] and [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] makes every affine open ring a G-ring and J-2, i.e. quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ alone covers $|X_1|$, so the glued formal scheme of [lem-per-formal-completion-reduction-dictionary] is $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I$. Its whole space is a formal affine open: $\widehat A_I$ is Noetherian and $I\widehat A_I$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Steps 1--4 therefore give quasi-excellence of $\widehat A_I$ and of the rings on all formal affine opens of $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I$. If $I=A$, the completion is the zero ring and the formal scheme is empty; if $I=0$, the completion is $A$. Nilpotent $I$ gives a stationary quotient tower; no case needs a separate argument.
